The police in Oyo State have arrested a serving police corporal and eight other suspects in separate operations involving alleged cultism and kidnapping. The Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, disclosed in a police operational success released on Thursday that operatives of the Command Monitoring Unit, Oyo Operational Base, raided a suspected Aiye Confraternity hideout on Sunday. He added that five suspects were arrested during the operation, including a policeman identified as Corporal Olayinka Oluwatobi, who was attached to MOPOL 72, Ago-Are, and seconded to Sports Eleyele, Ibadan, the state capital. He stated, “On 08/11/2026, operatives of the Command Monitoring Unit (Oyo Operational Base) carried out a coordinated raid on an Aiye Confraternity hideout. “Five suspects were arrested, including F/No. 538195 Cpl Olayinka Oluwatobi, who was attached to Mopol 72 Ago Are and seconded to Sports Eleyele, Ibadan. The case, according to the police spokesman, had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Ibadan for investigation. Eleyele River crossing: Safety can’t be left to luck S’West ADC stakeholders demand Aregbesola’s suspension Police probe suspected cult killing in Imo, hunt gunmen In a separate operation, Iniedu noted that operatives of the Command Monitoring Unit, working with the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, rescued one Abubakar Amidu at the Oteon/Odi Owo Forest on November 8. He noted that four suspects were arrested in connection with the abduction. He continued, “Abubakar Amidu, 30, who was abducted on 31/10/2026, was rescued unhurt at Oteon/Odi Owo Forest on 08/11/2026. The rescue operation was carried out by operatives of the Command Monitoring Unit and the Vigilante Group of Nigeria. “Four suspects were arrested, including Abdullahi Bello, Mohammed Kontagora, Alhaji Ali, and Usman Alhaji Ali.” Iniedu added that the victim’s mobile phone and the chain and lock allegedly used to restrain him were recovered during the operation. He concluded that investigation into the two incidents was ongoing, while efforts to track other possible suspects continued.
